stem: Meera looks at the stars from her rooftop in Jaipur at 9 p.m. in January. When she looks again at 9 p.m. in June, different stars are visible in the night sky. Which motion of the Earth causes this change in the stars seen at the same time of night?

options.text: the Earth rotating on its own axis
the Earth revolving around the Sun
the Moon revolving around the Earth
the Sun rotating on its own axis

teacher.key_rationale: The yearly change in the night sky at a fixed time of night is caused by Earth's revolution around the Sun, which shifts which part of space faces away from the Sun at 9 p.m. Rotation (A) causes the daily cycle, not the month-to-month change, and remains the trap for students swapping the sibling term rotation for revolution.
